Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that traveling a long distance to a high-volume center can have several benefits for patients with certain types of cancer. Specifically:

* Patients who traveled a long distance to a high-volume center had improved lymph node yield, neoadjuvant chemoradiation receipt, and 30- and 90-day mortality compared with those who traveled a short distance to a low-volume center.
* They also had improved 5-year survival.

This suggests that traveling to a high-volume center may be associated with better outcomes for patients with certain types of cancer. However, it's essential to note that the findings are based on control-for-factors analysis and may not capture all potential benefits of travel to a high-volume center.

It's also worth noting that the distance traveled is just one factor among many that can influence treatment outcomes. Other factors, such as patient factors (e.g., tumor characteristics), hospital factors (e.g., quality of care), and provider factors (e.g., expertise) may also play a role.

Overall, while traveling to a high-volume center may be associated with improved treatment outcomes for some patients, more research is needed to fully understand the relationship between distance and treatment efficacy.
